question: Can a job with no permissions and no cache action write the default-branch cache scope?
pass: Cannot (section 6), as the working rulings on #187 read it. A job of a workflow on a work branch of the canary, with permissions: {} and no cache action, is refused when it asks the cache API with its own GITHUB_TOKEN: listing the caches and deleting one both answer 403. What it writes through the runner's own cache service with its runtime token lands in the scope of its own ref and no other: the caches read through the Maintainer's login afterwards show ref refs/heads/trial/p-14 and none with ref refs/heads/main. It passes if both hold; if a write reaches the default branch's scope it fails, and section 4.9's assumption is amended by pull request.

body.words: The question and the ruling's condition are about a write, and it cannot be made: the API refuses the job's token (403), a run step is given no cache-service token, and no cache exists in any scope afterwards. One clause the session added to the ruling's condition did not hold: listing the caches answered 200, not 403, since a public repo's caches list is open to any token. It bears on reading, not on writing. A second clause the session added, that a write through the runner's cache service lands in its own ref's scope, could not be tried: a run step holds no such token, so no cache was written anywhere (none with the ref trial/p-14 either).
body.principle: The verdict follows the working rulings on #187, which read section 6's question; a clause the session added in the pass field is recorded here as held or not and does not decide the verdict.
